result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly explain that Helvetica Neue is missing on Windows and Android and that Windows renders text differently, and both say the renderer difference can't be fully removed. B gives a more sensible fallback chain (Segoe UI, Roboto, system-ui, sans-serif) and offers a system-stack option. Its test list is also more complete, covering zoom, Windows scaling, small body text and glyph coverage. A has extras like CORS and licensing but skips zoom and uses a thinner fallback stack. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B explains why the text looks different more completely: it covers macOS stem-darkening as well as Windows hinting, and notes that missing weights on old Android lead to synthesized bold. It also gives a proper CSS block and sets clear expectations at the end, including asking designers to review on Windows. A's test list is a little stronger, since it includes Windows scaling and browser text zoom, which B leaves out. Neither answer mentions light/dark mode.
